sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，在这个播客中，我们探讨二十岁时面临的一些重大生活改变和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界何地，很高兴你能来到这里收听新的一期节目。

sentences.en: Today, we are going to be talking about closure, what it is, what it isn't.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要探讨的是“释怀”——它是什么，它又不是什么。

sentences.en: It's very elusive nature, whether we need it and how to find yourself closure without needing another person's input or needing someone to have all the answers for you.
sentences.zh: 以及它那种极其难以捉摸的本质：我们是否需要释怀，以及如何在不需要他人介入或不需要别人为你提供所有答案的情况下，找到内心的释怀。

sentences.en: Closure, I think, is such an interesting concept in our 20s because there are so many storylines that we will live out,
sentences.zh: 我认为，在我们二十岁的时候，“释怀”是一个非常有趣的概念，因为我们将经历那么多的人生剧情，

sentences.en: so many relationships and situations that will not have a neat conclusion.
sentences.zh: 会有那么多的关系和状况无法迎来一个完美的结局。

sentences.en: As much as we might want them to, not every relationship is going to finish on a good note.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们可能很希望如此，但并非每一段关系都会以美好的结局收场。

sentences.en: Of course, when I talk about closure, most of us do think about relationships.
sentences.zh: 当然，当我谈到释怀时，我们大多数人想到的确实都是恋爱关系。

sentences.en: We think about love.
sentences.zh: 我们会想到爱情。

sentences.en: We think about that period after a relationship ends where we are left with thousands of questions.
sentences.zh: 我们会想到恋情结束后的那段时期，那时我们脑海中留下了成千上万个疑问。

sentences.en: Did they really love me?
sentences.zh: 他们真的爱过我吗？

sentences.en: What did I do wrong?
sentences.zh: 我做错了什么？

sentences.en: What do they think of me now?
sentences.zh: 他们现在是怎么看我的？

sentences.en: Why was I not enough?
sentences.zh: 为什么我还不够好？

sentences.en: Honestly, the list is endless.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这种问题列都列不完。

sentences.en: And I think the need for closure is a lot like grief.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，对释怀的需求在很大程度上就像是悲伤。

sentences.en: It is lost or misplaced love, a love that really lingers on.
sentences.zh: 那是失去或错付的爱，是一份挥之不去的爱。

sentences.en: But beyond those romantic relationships, we can also require closure at the end of platonic relationships and friendships.
sentences.zh: 但除了这些浪漫关系之外，我们在柏拉图式的关系和友情走到尽头时，也同样需要释怀。

sentences.en: I think friendships always seem to be painted as less important by our society, something that we just expect to follow along with us in life,
sentences.zh: 我觉得社会似乎总是把友情描绘成一种不那么重要的东西，觉得它只是我们在生活中顺其自然会相伴同行的一部分，

sentences.en: whilst our romantic relationships are really the main attraction.
sentences.zh: 而恋爱关系才是真正的重头戏。

sentences.en: But I really do truly believe that they can hurt so deeply when they come to an end.
sentences.zh: 但我真的坚信，当友情走向终结时，它所带来的痛苦可以同样深刻。

sentences.en: Probably because we never expect our friendships to end in that way.
sentences.zh: 这大概是因为我们从没想过我们的友情会以那种方式结束。

sentences.en: We never expect to go through a friendship breakup.
sentences.zh: 我们从没想过自己会经历朋友绝交。

sentences.en: Or, you know, I've heard so many stories of lifelong friendships where the other person suddenly goes to the friend or goes completely silent.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，我听过太多关于多年挚友突然对另一方不理不睬，或者彻底人间蒸发的故事。

sentences.en: Or friendship breakups that are so much worse than the heartbreak that we experience from romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 这种朋友间的决裂，有时候比我们在恋爱关系中经历的心碎还要痛苦得多。

sentences.en: When we are that connected with someone, when we spend so much time with them, we bond over everything, we talk all the time.
sentences.zh: 当我们和某人的联系如此紧密，花那么多时间陪伴彼此，无话不谈，什么都能聊的时候，

sentences.en: Seeing those connections, whether they are platonic or romantic, seeing them crumble is really upsetting,
sentences.zh: 看着这些羁绊——无论是柏拉图式的还是浪漫的——看着它们土崩瓦解，真的让人非常难过，

sentences.en: especially when we are left feeling very confused and unable to seek clarity.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当我们感到极度困惑，却又无法寻求一个明确的说法时。

sentences.en: In those moments, we want closure.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，我们渴望释怀。

sentences.en: We feel like it is the only thing that will help us come to terms with these events.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得那是唯一能帮助我们接受这些事情的东西。

sentences.en: But although we might want closure, do we really need it as much as we think we do?
sentences.zh: 但尽管我们可能渴望释怀，我们真的像自己想象的那样迫切需要它吗？

sentences.en: And when we say that we're looking for closure, what exactly does that entail?
sentences.zh: 当我们说我们在寻找释怀时，这究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: And is it maybe slightly naive for us to think that the person who caused us so much pain and disappointment is going to be the same person who can provide us with the answers
sentences.zh: 而且，如果我们以为那个带给我们无尽痛苦和失望的人，会反过来给我们提供能让自己疗愈的答案，

sentences.en: that will let us heal?
sentences.zh: 这会不会有点太天真了？

sentences.en: I don't necessarily think so.
sentences.zh: 我不认为一定如此。

sentences.en: So that's really what I want to focus on in today's episode.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是我想要在今天的节目中重点探讨的内容。

sentences.en: Do we need someone else to provide us with closure or can we provide it for ourselves?
sentences.zh: 我们是否需要别人来给我们提供释怀，还是说我们可以自己成全自己？

sentences.en: I think that my opinion is quite obvious.
sentences.zh: 我想我的观点已经很明显了。

sentences.en: But before we get into that, let's look into some of the psychological origins of this concept of closure and make sure that the foundations of our understanding are strong.
sentences.zh: 但在我们深入探讨之前，让我们先来了解一下“释怀”这一概念的一些心理学渊源，确保我们理解的根基足够牢固。

sentences.en: So closure essentially refers to our need to make sense of a situation and feel like it has a solid conclusion.
sentences.zh: 因此，释怀本质上指的是我们理清状况并感觉事情已经尘埃落定的心理需求。

sentences.en: In psychology, the need for closure is seen as a motivation to find an answer to an ambiguous
sentences.zh: 在心理学中，对释怀的需求被视为一种寻找模糊状况答案的动机，

sentences.en: situation, because as humans, as we know, we are not particularly good at navigating uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们所知，作为人类，我们并不太擅长应对不确定性。

sentences.en: So this motivation to find an answer, it is enhanced by what we see as the benefits of this, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，这种寻找答案的动机，会因为我们所看到的这些好处而得到强化，对吧？

sentences.en: So an increased ability to predict what might happen, being able to remove some of those fears, feeling certain of where we stand with someone.
sentences.zh: 比如增强了预测可能发生事情的能力，能够消除某些恐惧，对我们与某人的关系所处的位置感到确定。

sentences.en: Really, it's about finding a way and finding a place for these memories.
sentences.zh: 说到底，这是为了给这些记忆找到一种处理方式和归宿。

sentences.en: And social psychologists in particular suggest that people tend to have a need to view their
sentences.zh: 特别是社会心理学家指出，人们往往有一种需求，希望将自己的关系视为一个整体，

sentences.en: relationships as a whole, that they have, they are a complete story, they have a beginning, they have a middle, and they have an end.
sentences.zh: 觉得它们是一个完整的故事，有开头、有过程，也有结尾。

sentences.en: And when a relationship concludes, the mind seeks to fill in any gaps before moving on, so that it can find that ending.
sentences.zh: 而当一段关系结束时，大脑会试图在继续前行之前填补所有空白，以便找到那个结局。

sentences.en: In other words, we need that closure to essentially finish off the story.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们需要这种释怀来为这个故事画上句号。

sentences.en: And when we are left without an ending, either because the relationship ended quite abruptly, we didn't see it coming, you ended on a fight that you never
sentences.zh: 而当我们没有得到一个结局时——无论是由于关系结束得相当突然、我们始料未及、你们在一场从未解决的争吵中分手，

sentences.en: resolved, or there was just radio silence.
sentences.zh: 还是对方直接人间蒸发——

sentences.en: We don't know where to place that memory, because it still feels like it's ongoing.
sentences.zh: 我们就会不知道该把这段记忆放在哪里，因为它感觉还在继续。

sentences.en: It's an active storyline.
sentences.zh: 这是一个未完待续的故事线。

sentences.en: Our minds have this open chapter.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑里翻开着这样一个章节。

sentences.en: And this lack of a conclusion keeps us going back and returning again and again and again, wanting to find more answers by
sentences.zh: 这种缺乏结局的状态让我们不断地回想，一次又一次地沉溺其中，渴望通过翻找回忆来找到更多的答案，

sentences.en: searching through our memories, wanting to find a resting place for this relationship and for what it has become.
sentences.zh: 渴望为这段关系以及它最终的模样找到一个歇脚的归宿。

sentences.en: We all have, as humans, that individual drive for closure.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们每个人都有这种对释怀的内在驱动力。

sentences.en: But that need and that drive differs between us.
sentences.zh: 但这种需求和驱动力因人而异。

sentences.en: So mainly it differs in according to intensity and the intensity of our need for closure.
sentences.zh: 它主要根据我们的急切程度以及对释怀需求的强烈程度而有所不同。

sentences.en: This depends largely on our personality.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上取决于我们的性格。

sentences.en: So people with that intense need for closure, they may be used to being in control, and they prefer life to go as planned, they may feel really distressed,
sentences.zh: 因此，那些对释怀有着强烈需求的人，可能习惯了掌控一切，更喜欢生活按计划进行，他们可能会对不确定性感到非常痛苦，

sentences.en: by uncertainty, and might really challenge their sense of safety and well-being to not have the answers to a question.
sentences.zh: 无法对某个问题得到答案，可能会极大地挑战他们的安全感和幸福感。

sentences.en: And in the 1990s, these three psychologists actually came up with the need for
sentences.zh: 而在20世纪90年代，这三位心理学家实际上提出了“寻求释怀量表”，

sentences.en: closure scale, which can be used to really categorize people based on a number of questions, and determine
sentences.zh: 该量表可用于根据一系列问题真正对人群进行分类，并确定

sentences.en: where we kind of all sit on this spectrum of obtaining closure, what lengths we will go to find closure at the end of a relationship or at the end of some situation.
sentences.zh: 我们在获取释怀这一光谱上的大致位置，以及我们在一段关系或某种状况结束时会为了寻求释怀而付出多大的努力。

sentences.en: So those of us who really need closure, often make a lot of assumptions, or false judgments, or shut down as soon as a relationship is
sentences.zh: 因此，我们当中那些极其渴望释怀的人，往往会做出许多假设、错误的判断，或者在关系刚一结束时就立马关闭心扉，

sentences.en: over, in order to just provide ourselves with the ending without waiting around for someone else to come in
sentences.zh: 以便自己给自己一个结局，而不去苦等其他人来介入，

sentences.en: and challenge what we feel was the reason for this relationship not working, or what we feel was the reason that this had to end.
sentences.zh: 去反驳我们认为的导致这段关系破裂的原因，或者我们认为导致这一切不得不结束的原因。

sentences.en: The answers that we come up with, the conclusion that we reach, it's might, you know, it might not be entirely correct, it might be based on a lot of false premises.
sentences.zh: 我们得出的答案，我们所达到的结论，可能并不完全正确，它可能是建立在很多错误的前提之上的。

sentences.en: But at least in our minds, the story is over, we have a nice bookend to this relationship to this situation.
sentences.zh: 但至少在我们的脑海里，故事已经结束了，我们为这段关系、这种状况画上了一个漂亮的句号。

sentences.en: In contrast, sometimes we observe individuals who avoid closure, almost as a way to continue to suspend the relationship in space and time.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，有时我们会观察到一些刻意回避释怀的人，这几乎成了他们将这段关系悬置于时空之中的一种方式。

sentences.en: So the movie 500 Days of Summer, if you've, if you've seen it, and if you haven't, you really should go and watch it, it's quite good.
sentences.zh: 比如电影《和莎莫的500天》，如果你看过的话——如果没有看过的化，你真的应该去看看，拍得挺不错的。

sentences.en: But this movie, cult classic, it's an excellent example of someone who does not have a high need for closure, in fact, avoids closure.
sentences.zh: 但这部电影，作为一部经典邪典电影，是一个对释怀没有强烈需求、甚至主动回避释怀的绝佳例子。

sentences.en: So Tom, the main character, he really remains suspended in the happy memories of the relationship, and he is fixated on them, almost as a way to stay connected with his ex.
sentences.zh: 男主角汤姆，他 realmente（其实应为really，译文保持流畅）沉浸在这段关系的美好回忆中无法自拔，并且对它们执念很深，这几乎成了他与前女友保持联系的一种方式。

sentences.en: Closure signifies the end.
sentences.zh: 释怀标志着结束。

sentences.en: But if you are still anticipating something more, if you are unable to rectify your feelings for someone, even when you
sentences.zh: 但如果你还在期待更多，如果你即使明知该向前看了却仍无法理顺自己对某人的感情，如果你还抱有可能会复合的期待，

sentences.en: know it's time to move on, if you have these expectations that you might get back together,
sentences.zh: 有时你其实是在不断剥夺自己释怀的机会，以此来让自己停留在关系的无限可能中。

sentences.en: sometimes you actually continue to deprive yourself of closure, in order to stay in the potential of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们在某些情况下对逃避释怀的固有需求，是由我们想要避开随之而来的负面后果的愿望所控制的。

sentences.en: That's because our innate need to avoid closure in some of these instances is controlled by our desire to avoid the negative consequences that come along with that.
sentences.zh: 因此，举个例子，一旦你承认了“是的，这段关系结束了，这个人不想跟我说话，我也不想跟他们说话”，完全承认这一点就意味着你必须开始处理这对你意味着什么，以及随之而来的痛苦。

sentences.en: So, for example, once you acknowledge that, yes, this relationship is over, this person does not want
sentences.zh: 所以我们把事情久久拖延，以此来逃避这一点。

sentences.en: to talk to me, I do not want to talk to them, acknowledging that fully means that you have to start processing what that means for you, the pain that that might bring.
sentences.zh: 其实这还有一个挺有趣的小方面，算是本集的一个趣味冷知识。

sentences.en: So we elongate the situation in order to avoid that.
sentences.zh: 人们——这类真正没有那种释怀需求的人，人们对这在其余性格中到底意味着什么做过一些研究，他们发现，

sentences.en: There's actually another little interesting facet of this that is kind of the fun fact for this episode.
sentences.zh: 在针对寻求释怀与创造力水平之间相关性所进行的一些研究中，那些回避释怀的人明显更具创造力。

sentences.en: People, these types of people who don't really have that need for closure, they've done some studies on what that really means for the rest of their personality, and they found
sentences.zh: 也许这是因为他们对深层情感的欣赏，或者是因为他们更能泰然处之地面临充满不确定性的事物。

sentences.en: that, and some studies conducted on the correlation between the need for closure and creativity levels, people who avoid closure are significantly more creative.
sentences.zh: 所以他们能够把这种不确定性和那种开放式的结局转化到他们的艺术或他们的创作中去。

sentences.en: Maybe that's because of their appreciation of deep emotions, or the fact that they are more comfortable with things being uncertain.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的冷知识，但这并不是说我们在无意识或其他情况下剥夺自己的释怀就全是好事、有很多好处。

sentences.en: So they're able to transfer that uncertainty and that kind of open-endedness into their art or what they're creating.
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为，我们中的很多人最终都会达到这样一个点——即使你对释怀的需求很低，我们也确实会达到一个点，

sentences.en: So a little fun fact, that's not to say that depriving ourselves of closure, either unconsciously or not, is all good and has a lot of benefits.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们再也无法活在过去了。也许我们缺乏释怀正在阻碍我们向前看，或者它让我们处于一种极度缺乏情感投入的状态。

sentences.en: I actually think that a lot of us do get to a point, even if you have a low need for closure, we do get to a point
sentences.zh: 我认为我们经常在刚结束长期关系的人身上看到这一点，他们其实还没弄明白这段关系为什么没有走到最后。

sentences.en: where we can no longer live in the paSt. And maybe our lack of closure is preventing us from moving on, or it is keeping us in a very emotionally unavailable place.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他们不一定知道或许需要改变什么，但更多时候，你的一只脚依然陷在那段过去的感情里，

sentences.en: I think we commonly see this with people straight out of a long-term relationship, who actually haven't yet figured out exactly why the relationship didn't work.
sentences.zh: 占用了本可以投入到其他事情上的情感、精神和心理空间。

sentences.en: Because of that, they don't necessarily know what maybe needs to change, but more often than not, you still have one foot stuck in that past relationship,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是对另一个人，而是为了其他事情。

sentences.en: taking up emotional, mental, and psychological space that might be better devoted for something else.
sentences.zh: 而且这超级烦人。

sentences.en: Not just to someone else, but for something else.
sentences.zh: 我之前稍微聊过这个，几年前我和某个人有过一段奇怪的暧昧不清的关系，那真是太消磨情感了。

sentences.en: And it's super frustrating.
sentences.zh: 太令人心力交瘁了。

sentences.en: I've talked about this a bit before, but I had this weird situationship a few years back with someone, and it was so emotionally exhausting.
sentences.zh: 它把我的精神状态搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: It was draining.
sentences.zh: 我毫无自信可言。

sentences.en: It left me in such a bad place mentally.
sentences.zh: 我几乎没法跟任何人说话，我花了大量的时间才恢复过来，花了大量时间去寻找我所需要的内心平静与释怀，

sentences.en: I had no self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 这甚至比我结束上一段长期感情时花的时间还要多。

sentences.en: I could barely speak to anybody, and it took me so much time to recover, and so much time to find that
sentences.zh: 原因就在于留下了太多的“如果”。

sentences.en: peace and closure that I needed, more so than when I'd ended my previous long-term relationship.
sentences.zh: 至少在我的恋爱关系里，我们多少还有机会真正把这种羁绊走到它的终点站，如果可以这么说的话。

sentences.en: And the reason why was because of how many what-ifs were left over.
sentences.zh: 就像我们把注定要经历的旅程过完了一样。

sentences.en: At least in my relationship, we kind of had the chance to really take this connection to its final destination, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 我们曾试图让它走通。

sentences.en: Like, we lived out the journey that we were meant to go on.
sentences.zh: 但没能成功，已经没什么好说的了。

sentences.en: We had tried to make it work.
sentences.zh: 也没什么好做的了。

sentences.en: It didn't, there was nothing left to say.
sentences.zh: 无需多言。

sentences.en: There was nothing left to do.
sentences.zh: 尘埃落定。

sentences.en: The end of the story was written very quickly.
sentences.zh: 故事的结局写得非常快。

sentences.en: But with that situationship, because the entire relationship had been so tumultuous, the conclusion, or what I thought was the conclusion, was equally confusing.
sentences.zh: 但对于那种暧昧不清的关系，因为整段感情实在是太动荡了，所以结局——或者说我认为的结局——同样让人困惑。

sentences.en: You know, was it me?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，是我的问题吗？

sentences.en: Was it him?
sentences.zh: 是他的问题吗？

sentences.en: Was it just circumstances?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是环境使然吗？

sentences.en: Was it timing?
sentences.zh: 是时机不对吗？

sentences.en: In hindsight, I really can't believe I spent so much time, so many months thinking about this person, but I also realized that there
sentences.zh: 事后回想起来，我真的不敢相信自己居然花了那么多时间、好几个月去想着这个人，但我也意识到

sentences.en: were some parts of that relationship that always meant I was never going to get the answers that I needed at the end.
sentences.zh: 这段感情中总有一些部分，注定让我无法在最后得到我需要的答案。

sentences.en: Or so I thought.
sentences.zh: 或者我以前是这么认为的。

sentences.en: I think when we are in this moment of grief and ambiguity and sadness, we like to believe in the idea of a quick fix, and we fixate on this premise that there is
sentences.zh: 我想，当我们处于这种悲伤、迷茫和痛苦的时刻时，我们倾向于相信存在某种快速解决的办法，并且执着于这样一个前提：

sentences.en: something we don't know that can explain it all away.
sentences.zh: 有些我们不知道的事，可以把这一切都解释清楚。

sentences.en: And take away all these feelings, there is some answer out there that's going to make us feel better.
sentences.zh: 并且带走所有这些情绪，总会有某个答案能让我们感觉好受一些。

sentences.en: And we place a lot of hope in someone else's ability to reach our emotional conclusions for us.
sentences.zh: 我们把太多的希望寄托在别人替我们做出情感总结的能力上。

sentences.en: I think we obviously all need closure.
sentences.zh: 我想我们显然都需要一个了断。

sentences.en: It is a human need.
sentences.zh: 这是一种人类的需求。

sentences.en: But we don't necessarily need someone else to give it to us.
sentences.zh: 但我们不一定非要别人来给我们这个了断。

sentences.en: Our solution to the closure problem doesn't always lie with our ex or a former friend or any explanation that they can provide us.
sentences.zh: 我们解决“了断”问题的方法，并不总是取决于前任、曾经的朋友，或是他们能提供的任何解释。

sentences.en: In fact, I think you are probably the only person who is going to be able to bring that for yourself, even if you don't realize it in the moment.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我觉得你可能才是那个唯一能为自己带来这一切的人，即使你当下并没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: In hindsight, nothing that someone else has said has made you feel any better.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，别人说过的话并没有让你感觉好过一点。

sentences.en: Normally, it's just that you have been able to integrate that into your idea of the relationship and your idea of the conclusion and write that ending for yourself.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，只是因为你已经能够将那些话融入到你对这段感情的看法、对结局的看法中，并为你自己写下了那个结局。

sentences.en: So there's a few reasons why I don't think that we should rely on other people to bring us closure.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为我们不应该指望别人来给我们一个了断，原因有以下几个。

sentences.en: Firstly, their actions were in some ways the closure that you needed, their inability to treat you with
sentences.zh: 首先，他们的行为在某种程度上就是你需要的了断，他们无法用

sentences.en: respect or their fickleness, their inconsistency, their cruelty, even at times.
sentences.zh: 尊重对待你，或者他们的反复无常、前后不一，甚至有时表现出的残酷。

sentences.en: That is really the evidence that all along, this person did not have the emotional maturity to navigate an adult relationship with you, right?
sentences.zh: 这才是真正的证据，证明这个人自始至终都不具备与你进行成年人恋爱交往的情感成熟度，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, a lot of the time, if you are left without answers at the end of a relationship, something has kind of not gone wrong, but there is something that they could have
sentences.zh: 就像很多时候，如果你在一段感情结束时没有得到答案，倒也不是说出了什么大问题，而是有些他们本可以

sentences.en: provided you that they could have spoken to about along the way that they chose not to.
sentences.zh: 提供给你的东西、本可以在过程中跟你沟通的事情，他们选择了不说。

sentences.en: And I think secondly, like I mentioned before, you are relying on the same person who hurt you in the first place
sentences.zh: 我想其次，就像我之前提到的，你竟然指望那个最初伤害你的人

sentences.en: to heal that very wound that they created, either intentionally or unintentionally.
sentences.zh: 来治愈他们无论是故意还是无意间造成的伤口。

sentences.en: I think the irony of this is best understood, you know, through metaphor.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种讽刺通过隐喻最容易理解。

sentences.en: If you fall off a ladder and you break your back, you are not going to climb back up that same ladder with the hope that you will fall off it again
sentences.zh: 如果你从梯子上摔下来摔断了背，你不会再爬上同一个梯子，指望着自己会再次摔下来

sentences.en: and break your back back to the way that it was before.
sentences.zh: 然后把背摔回原来的样子。

sentences.en: Do you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, this person has obviously created some pain and has injured you in some way.
sentences.zh: 就像这个人显然带来了一些痛苦，并在某种程度上伤害了你。

sentences.en: I don't necessarily think that they can undo that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们一定能弥补这一点。

sentences.en: They might not even have the answer that you want because they don't know it themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能没有你想要的答案，因为他们自己也不知道。

sentences.en: They may not even be able to articulate their actual feelings well enough to provide you with the clarity that you need.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能无法足够好地表达自己真实的情感，来为你提供你所需要的清晰认知。

sentences.en: And there's also no guarantee that they're going to be honest with you either.
sentences.zh: 而且也没有人能保证他们会对你诚实。

sentences.en: So you are relying on a faulty or an unwilling messenger for your emotional and mental sanity.
sentences.zh: 所以为了你的情感和心理健康，你居然在依仗一个不可靠或者不情愿的传话人。

sentences.en: I also saw this really beautiful quote the other day that I think expresses this very well.
sentences.zh: 前几天我还看到了一句非常美妙的话，我觉得它很好地表达了这一点。

sentences.en: Life is short.
sentences.zh: 生命短暂。

sentences.en: I don't think that you should wait around for apologies.
sentences.zh: 我认为你不应该苦苦等待道歉。

sentences.en: Your peace is worth more than their acknowledgement.
sentences.zh: 你的内心平静比他们的承认更有价值。

sentences.en: If you're looking for them to say sorry, if you're looking for them to not just apologize but make some kind of amends, I don't think you're ever going to truly believe that
sentences.zh: 如果你期望他们说对不起，如果你期望他们不仅道歉，还能做出某种弥补，我觉得你无论如何也不会真正相信

sentences.en: anyways.
sentences.zh: 这一切。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's going to undo anything that has already happened.
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为这无法抹杀已经发生过的任何事情。

sentences.en: At least they won't be able to undo it once again.
sentences.zh: 至少他们无法再次抹杀这一切了。

sentences.en: Sadly, it's back to you.
sentences.zh: 可悲的是，一切又回到了你身上。

sentences.en: And thirdly, and for me personally, this is the most important reason we shouldn't rely on others for closure, is that sometimes we use
sentences.zh: 第三点，对个人而言这也是我们不应指望别人来给个了断的最重要原因，那就是有时我们会把

sentences.en: closure as a proxy for something else that we actually want.
sentences.zh: “了断”当作我们真正想要的某种其他东西的借口。

sentences.en: We think that we need to reach out to them just one more time, grab a coffee with them just once more in order to get closure.
sentences.zh: 我们以为自己需要再联系他们一次，再跟他们喝一次咖啡，只是为了做个了断。

sentences.en: But really, what you want to do is just see them again because you're not ready to move on.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你只是想再见他们一面，因为你还没准备好往前走。

sentences.en: But you're evoking this idea of closure as an excuse.
sentences.zh: 但你却把“了断”这个概念搬出来当借口。

sentences.en: I'm not trying to call you out.
sentences.zh: 我不是想当众戳穿你。

sentences.en: I'm just saying from experience, I would do this.
sentences.zh: 我只是根据经验说，我以前也会这样做。

sentences.en: I'd be like, oh, you know, I just have a few more questions about the end of our relationship.
sentences.zh: 我会说，哦，你知道的，我只是对我们感情的结束还有几个问题要问。

sentences.en: But really, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我根本没有。

sentences.en: I knew everything that I needed to know.
sentences.zh: 我该知道的都知道了。

sentences.en: I just wanted to see them.
sentences.zh: 我只是想见见他们。

sentences.en: You have convinced yourself that you have good intentions, when actually underneath this urge is a true desire to reconnect.
sentences.zh: 你总是说服自己说你怀揣善意，而实际上这种冲动背后是对重新建立联系的真实渴望。

sentences.en: And this pattern is keeping you stuck in the memories of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 这种模式让你深陷这段感情的回忆中无法自拔。

sentences.en: It's making you feel like it's not quite over yet, that there's more to come.
sentences.zh: 它让你觉得好像还没真正结束，后面还有故事。

sentences.en: You're left kind of discussing your relationship with this person.
sentences.zh: 你最终陷入了跟这个人讨论你们感情的境地。

sentences.en: You're looking for answers that you know they can never give you.
sentences.zh: 你在寻找那些你深知他们永远无法给你的答案。

sentences.en: And when you repeatedly go back to this person with more excuses to catch up, you are in the closure cycle.
sentences.zh: 当你带着更多叙旧的借口一次次回到这个人身边时，你就陷入了“了断循环”中。

sentences.en: We are not letting the connection fade away from our memory and our brains.
sentences.zh: 我们没有让这种联系从我们的记忆和大脑中渐渐淡去。

sentences.en: So in psychology, particularly in cognitive psychology, there is this idea known as long-term potentiation.
sentences.zh: 所以在心理学中，特别是在认知心理学中，有一个被称为“长时程增强”的概念。

sentences.en: And it has to do with how our neurons make and replace connections and pathways in the brain.
sentences.zh: 它与我们的神经元如何在头脑中建立和替换连接与通路有关。

sentences.en: So the more we use a connection, for example, the more we talk to someone and see them and interact with them and bond with them, the more we use it, the stronger that
sentences.zh: 因此，我们使用某种连接越多，例如我们越是和某人交谈、见面、互动、建立羁绊，我们用得越多，那种

sentences.en: neural connection becomes.
sentences.zh: 神经连接就会变得越强。

sentences.en: When that relationship disappears, the neural pathway is not stimulated as much by an external presence or stimuli.
sentences.zh: 当这段关系消失时，神经通路受外部存在或刺激的激活就会减少。

sentences.en: So it's used less and less until it begins to fade and be replaced inevitably by something that is more important.
sentences.zh: 所以它用得越来越少，直到开始消退，并不可避免地被更重要的东西所取代。

sentences.en: That is a natural part of the recovery process, specifically after the end of a relationship.
sentences.zh: 这是恢复过程的自然部分，特别是在一段感情结束之后。

sentences.en: It's the reason why we say that time heals because it quite literally does.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们说时间能治愈一切，因为它的确字面意义上能治愈一切。

sentences.en: It heals us by letting our brain do what it does best, which is prioritize what is important and what is not important.
sentences.zh: 它通过让大脑做它最擅长的事情来治愈我们，那就是区分什么是重要的，什么是不重要的。

sentences.en: And if this person is no longer part of your life, we want our brain to deprioritize the information that it has about this individual.
sentences.zh: 如果这个人不再是你生活的一部分，我们希望大脑降低对这个人的相关信息的优先处理级。

sentences.en: When we continue to find opportunities to talk to them, to reach out, to call, see this person, all we are doing is keeping this connection alive.
sentences.zh: 当我们继续寻找机会跟他们说话、联系、打电话、见这个人时，我们所做的一切只是在让这种联系保持活生生的状态。

sentences.en: We are keeping it strong.
sentences.zh: 我们在让它保持强韧。

sentences.en: We are keeping that pathway and those memories present.
sentences.zh: 我们在让那条通路和那些记忆持续存在。

sentences.en: And we aren't letting ourselves move on the way that we should.
sentences.zh: 我们没有让自己以应有的方式向前迈进。

sentences.en: This neural explanation is not to claim that you shouldn't reach out if you really need to, but I do believe that one closure conversation is probably enough.
sentences.zh: 这种神经学上的解释并不是说如果你真的有需要就一定不能联系，但我确实相信，一次了断的对话大概就足够了。

sentences.en: You have a right to ask for closure, but you need to ensure that you want it for the right reasons.
sentences.zh: 你有权要求做个了断，但你需要确保你的动机是正确的。

sentences.en: And I also don't think you should expect to leave the conversation feeling completely sure of yourself and renewed.
sentences.zh: 而且我也不认为你应该指望在结束对话时感到彻底的心安理得和焕然一新。

sentences.en: Those expectations once again contribute to the closure seeking cycle.
sentences.zh: 这些期望再次助长了寻求了断的循环。

sentences.en: Because when you go into it thinking,
sentences.zh: 因为当你带着这样的想法去沟通时：

sentences.en: I just need to hear this one thing and I'll be okay.
sentences.zh: “我只需要听到这一句话，我就会没事了。”

sentences.en: It's never just that one thing that you need to hear.
sentences.zh: 你需要的从来都不是那单单的一句话。

sentences.en: And so you'll keep going back, wanting more and more, waiting for the right thing to be said when it won't be said at all.
sentences.zh: 所以你会不断回头，想要获得更多，等待着那句永远不会说出口的正确的话出现。

sentences.en: So when going into that conversation, if you choose to have a closure chat, make sure firstly that you have a time limit.
sentences.zh: 因此，在进入那场对话时，如果你选择进行一次了断的畅谈，首先要确保设定一个时间限制。

sentences.en: Do not find yourself talking to them for six, seven, eight hours, staying over, you know, going for a long drive.
sentences.zh: 不要不知不觉跟他们聊了六、七、八个小时，留宿过夜，你知道的，还去兜风。

sentences.en: Like don't find yourself in a situation that is reminiscent of your relationship.
sentences.zh: 不要让自己陷入那种会勾起对过去恋情回忆的境地。

sentences.en: You need to have your questions ready and you need to have your intentions clear.
sentences.zh: 你需要准备好你的问题，并且让你的意图保持清晰。

sentences.en: What are you actually hoping to get out of this?
sentences.zh: 你到底希望从中得到什么？

sentences.en: Is there actually a reason that you need to be there right now and you need to be discussing this with them?
sentences.zh: 真的有什么原因让你此刻必须呆在那里，必须和他们讨论这些吗？

sentences.en: Remember as well that this is also a controlled conversation.
sentences.zh: 同时也要记住，这也是一场受到控制的对话。

sentences.en: This is not a time to try and get them back.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个试图挽回对方的时机。

sentences.en: It's not a time to bring up old arguments.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个翻旧账的时机。

sentences.en: This is a space for understanding and moving forward.
sentences.zh: 这是一个用于理解并向前看的空间。

sentences.en: It's also important to acknowledge that there are a lot of situations where we are not provided with that opportunity to talk it through with someone else.
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是我们要承认，在很多情况下，我们并没有机会跟别人把事情谈清楚。

sentences.en: Especially in some of those situations that we spoke of before where the other person has just chosen to break all contact.
sentences.zh: 特别是在我们之前提到的一些情况下，对方只是选择切断所有联系。

sentences.en: They've chosen to block you, to ghost you and this might sound controversial but as hard as that is, that is their right to do.
sentences.zh: 他们选择把你拉黑、对你冷暴力，这听起来可能有点争议，但尽管这很难接受，那是他们的权利。

sentences.en: I usually see these situations in friendships when someone has actually just been unable to set boundaries or communicate.
sentences.zh: 我通常在友情中看到这种情况，当某人实际上就是无法设定边界或进行沟通时。

sentences.en: Maybe they are very conflict averse.
sentences.zh: 也许他们非常抗拒冲突。

sentences.en: So something has been bothering them for a while, they just don't know how to talk to you about it.
sentences.zh: 所以有些事困扰了他们一段时间，他们只是不知道该怎么跟你谈。

sentences.en: You remain unaware.
sentences.zh: 而你对此一无所知。

sentences.en: It's not like you've done anything wrong.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你做错了什么。

sentences.en: Maybe you have but you just haven't been given an opportunity to rectify the situation or to apologize.
sentences.zh: 也许你确实做错了，但你根本没有机会纠正错误或道歉。

sentences.en: And so this person eventually snaps and their only option they see in their mind is to just go completely no contact with you.
sentences.zh: 所以这个人最终情绪崩溃，在他们脑海中唯一的选择就是彻底和你断绝联系。

sentences.en: I know it doesn't feel fair that we are left to navigate the aftermath of this ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们要自己去收拾这种残局，这让人感觉很不公平。

sentences.en: But we cannot control what other people see as best for them.
sentences.zh: 但我们无法控制别人认为对他们最有利的是什么。

sentences.en: What you can control is what you do next.
sentences.zh: 你能控制的是你接下来要做什么。

sentences.en: And I think it's your turn to do what's best for you and to find a way to move forward and provide yourself once again with closure.
sentences.zh: 我想现在轮到你去做对你自己最有利的事了，去寻找一条前进的道路，再次为自己做个了断。

sentences.en: So that is what I want to discuss next.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我接下来要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: How do we find closure without reliance on others?
sentences.zh: 如何在不依赖别人的情况下找到内心的了断？

sentences.en: How do we move on successfully?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能成功地向前看？

sentences.en: Doing it all by ourselves, officially closing a chapter in this book, is not going to come without some challenges.
sentences.zh: 完全靠我们自己去完成，正式合上这本书里的一章，这个过程并非一帆风顺。

sentences.en: I know this all too well.
sentences.zh: 这一点我深有体会。

sentences.en: I'm sure that you do as well if you're listening to this episode.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在收听这一期节目，我确信你也深有同感。

sentences.en: And there are so many times where we sit back and I think just wish and pray that we could be over it by now.
sentences.zh: 有太多次我们向后靠去，我想我们只是在许愿和祈祷，希望现在就已经翻篇了。

sentences.en: We just want to be over it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想要彻底走出来。

sentences.en: We're ready to just have moved on.
sentences.zh: 我们随时准备着翻篇。

sentences.en: But sometimes we're also not willing to do the work to get there because the path through is
sentences.zh: 但有时我们也不愿为达成这一目标付出努力，因为通往那里的道路

sentences.en: often, you know, the path that is hardeSt. But I have five tips and kind of pieces of instruction for you.
sentences.zh: 通常——你知道的——是一条更艰难的路。不过，我有五个建议和一些指导供你参考。

sentences.en: And I think following this process releases a lot of the grief and the anguish that otherwise keeps us quite trapped in the past and quite trapped in the closure cycle.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，遵循这个过程可以释放大量的悲伤和痛苦，否则我们会被紧紧困在过去和闭环的死胡同里。

sentences.en: So my tips are as follows.
sentences.zh: 所以我的建议如下。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about changing your mindset around what the end of this relationship has brought you.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈谈如何改变你的心态，来看待这段关系的结束为你带来了什么。

sentences.en: Second, how to not be afraid of negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 第二，如何不害怕负面情绪。

sentences.en: Thirdly, how not to be afraid of memory flare-ups.
sentences.zh: 第三，如何不害怕记忆突然闪现。

sentences.en: How to take responsibility.
sentences.zh: 如何承担责任。

sentences.en: And then finally, how to release the pain that is wanting you to go back and ask more questions and look for more answers.
sentences.zh: 最后，如何释放那个促使你想回头问更多问题、寻找更多答案的痛苦。

sentences.en: And I have a specific exercise for this that I think is so important.
sentences.zh: 为此我有一个具体的练习，我认为这非常重要。

sentences.en: It has been so helpful to me in those times that I really needed closure.
sentences.zh: 在我极度需要内心理清的时候，它对我非常有帮助。

sentences.en: So to begin, let's talk about changing your mindset.
sentences.zh: 那么首先，我们来谈谈改变心态。

sentences.en: We hear this a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们经常听到这种说法。

sentences.en: And I understand that when we hear this, people talk about mindset shifts and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 我也理解，当我们听到这些时，大家都在讨论心态转变之类的事情。

sentences.en: It's very easy to dismiss this and just be like, that is a, that is nonsense.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易对此不屑一顾，觉得这纯粹是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: That it's a bunch of garbage.
sentences.zh: 觉得这是一堆垃圾。

sentences.en: Like, let's just skip this step.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们直接跳过这一步吧。

sentences.en: I don't need to change my mindset.
sentences.zh: 我不需要改变心态。

sentences.en: It's just a terrible situation.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是个糟糕透顶的局面。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: And in many ways, it is a terrible situation.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这确实是一个糟糕透顶的局面。

sentences.en: But we're going to trust the psychology on this.
sentences.zh: 但我们要相信这方面的心理学。

sentences.en: And the psychology says that we have control over our cognitions and our thoughts about a situation.
sentences.zh: 心理学表明，我们能够控制自己对某种情况的认知和想法。

sentences.en: And these cognitions can be changed to better suit us.
sentences.zh: 这些认知是可以改变的，以更好地适应我们的需求。

sentences.en: So instead of sitting there and thinking, this is the worst thing that has ever happened to me.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其坐在那里想，这是我经历过的最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: This is so terrible.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I'm never going to recover from this.
sentences.zh: 我永远也走不出来了。

sentences.en: I'm never going to find love again.
sentences.zh: 我再也不会找到真爱了。

sentences.en: I'm never going to have a friend as good as her.
sentences.zh: 我再也找不到像她那么好的朋友了。

sentences.en: This is the end for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说一切都完了。

sentences.en: Replace those thoughts deliberately with ones that suit you better.
sentences.zh: 不如刻意用更适合你的想法来替换这些念头。

sentences.en: Yes, it sucks.
sentences.zh: 没错，这很烂。

sentences.en: But this ending was a gift.
sentences.zh: 但这个结局是一份礼物。

sentences.en: This has given me things that I wouldn't have imagined for myself.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了我许多以前从未想象过的东西。

sentences.en: What doors are opening because that relationship ended?
sentences.zh: 因为这段关系的结束，有哪些门正在为你打开？

sentences.en: What is it teaching you about yourself?
sentences.zh: 它教会了你关于自己的什么？

sentences.en: I always say that the best beginnings are truly hidden in the endings of things.
sentences.zh: 我总是说，最好的开始其实就隐藏在事物的结局之中。

sentences.en: Because it's there that the story really gets to take like so many different turns.
sentences.zh: 因为正是在那里，故事才真正迎来了如此之多的不同转折。

sentences.en: It's where the storyline is most open for change.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，故事线对改变最为开放。

sentences.en: That's the point that you're at right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是你目前所处的状态。

sentences.en: I think stop those negative thoughts and replace them with a deliberate thought.
sentences.zh: 我认为应该制止那些消极的想法，并用一个刻意的想法取而代之。

sentences.en: So when you think, I just want to get over this.
sentences.zh: 所以当你想到，我只想快点摆脱这一切。

sentences.en: I'm so, this is just the worst thing that's ever happened to me.
sentences.zh: 我太……这简直是我经历过最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Stop and say, this might be the best thing that's ever happened to me.
sentences.zh: 停下来，对自己说，这可能是我经历过最好的事情。

sentences.en: I just can't see it yet.
sentences.zh: 我只是现在还看不到。

sentences.en: I just don't know what my future looks like.
sentences.zh: 我只是不知道我的未来会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And that is really exciting.
sentences.zh: 而这真的让人兴奋。

sentences.en: When you continue to interrupt those negative thoughts and replace them, that repetition will mean that you get to a point someday where it becomes automatic.
sentences.zh: 当你不断打断这些消极想法并用新想法替换它们时，这种重复意味着总有一天你会达到一种让它变成自动反应的地步。

sentences.en: You don't need to try and convince yourself.
sentences.zh: 你不需要努力去说服自己。

sentences.en: You just believe it.
sentences.zh: 你就是深信不疑。

sentences.en: You just believe that maybe this happened not for a reason, but there is something that is going to come out of this that you would have missed if that relationship had continued.
sentences.zh: 你只是相信，也许这件事发生并非出于某种原因，但它会带给你一些成果——如果这段关系继续下去，你就会错过这些。

sentences.en: I really think that understanding that and having a more positive, not just positive, but a different mindset towards the end of a relationship, towards
sentences.zh: 我真的认为，理解这一点并对关系的结束抱有一种更积极的、不仅是积极的、而是不同的心态，朝着

sentences.en: the need for closure, gets us to a point where we are not scared to let ourselves move on.
sentences.zh: 对内心理清（closure）的需求，能让我们达到不再害怕让自己继续前行的状态。

sentences.en: And this is where the next step comes in.
sentences.zh: 而这就是接下来这一步发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: True closure is about facing, unfortunately, negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 真正的内心释怀，不幸的是，就是要面对负面情绪。

sentences.en: And sometimes what keeps us in the memories of a relationship, what keeps us going back, what
sentences.zh: 有时，是什么让我们深陷于一段关系的记忆中无法自拔，是什么让我们不断回头，是什么

sentences.en: keeps us unable to move on, is knowing that the next step after that is going to be really painful.
sentences.zh: 让我们无法前行，是因为我们知道接下来的那一步将会非常痛苦。

sentences.en: Once we acknowledge that the relationship is truly over, that there is no more that they can provide
sentences.zh: 一旦我们承认这段关系真的结束了，他们再也无法提供

sentences.en: us that is going to make us feel better, there is no more bargaining, that is going to naturally trigger a lot of grief.
sentences.zh: 任何能让我们感觉好一点的东西，不再有任何讨价还价，这自然会引发大量的悲伤。

sentences.en: And so we engage in avoidance.
sentences.zh: 因此我们选择了逃避。

sentences.en: But when we allow ourselves to realize that, you know, true closure is about facing these negative emotions, there will be hard times.
sentences.zh: 但当我们开始意识到，你知道的，真正的释怀就是去直面这些负面情绪时，困难的时期总会过去。

sentences.en: When we no longer avoid the tears, we no longer avoid the fears about the future, the anxieties, the dark emotions, but we find an outlet for that energy.
sentences.zh: 当我们不再逃避眼泪，不再逃避对未来的恐惧、焦虑和黑暗情绪，而是为这种能量找到一个宣泄口时。

sentences.en: I really think that we get to a closer point of being able to live with these past experiences and the knowledge that they didn't work out.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为，我们会离坦然接受这些过往经历以及它们最终无果而终的事实更近一步。

sentences.en: It is not as scary as it has to be.
sentences.zh: 它并没有想象中那么可怕。

sentences.en: I also want to reassure you that subconsciously, unconsciously thinking about this person, having them pop into your head does not mean that you are not ready to move on.
sentences.zh: 我也想向你保证，潜意识里、无意识地去想这个人，让他们突然闯入你的脑海，并不意味着你还没有准备好向前看。

sentences.en: Do not confuse that with a need to reach back out to this person.
sentences.zh: 不要把这误认为是你需要重新联系这个人的信号。

sentences.en: It is totally entirely normal to still have the occasional thought about them, especially if you've been with this person for a long time, or they are a friend who has been with
sentences.zh: 偶尔还会想起他们，这完全、绝对是正常的，特别是如果你和这个人在一起很长时间，或者他们是陪伴了你

sentences.en: you for your whole life, or the situation you're trying to find closure from was particularly upsetting or traumatic or really frustrating.
sentences.zh: 一生的朋友，或者你试图从中释怀的处境特别令人心烦、痛苦或极其沮丧。

sentences.en: It takes a while for that memory to be dulled and to feel like it has a place.
sentences.zh: 这些记忆需要一段时间才会逐渐淡去，并在心中找到合适的位置。

sentences.en: I think we all know that weird feeling where you wake up after a dream that you've had about someone, and you haven't seen them for months.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都有一种奇怪的感觉，就是在做了一个关于某人的梦之后醒来，而你已经几个月没见过他们了。

sentences.en: And suddenly, there they are popping up in your subconscious.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们就出现在你的潜意识里。

sentences.en: Or strangely, you just can't stop thinking about the things that you did, you know, two summers ago.
sentences.zh: 或者奇怪的是，你就是忍不住去想你做过的事，你知道的，就是两年前的夏天。

sentences.en: You can't stop thinking about the situation.
sentences.zh: 你满脑子都是那种情境。

sentences.en: These are called memory flare-ups, and they are totally normal.
sentences.zh: 这些被称为记忆闪现，它们完全是正常的。

sentences.en: Especially when we are dreaming, our brain just tends to fire off a lot of random energy, and that sparks old connections, old paths, old feelings.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在我们做梦的时候，我们的大脑往往会释放出大量随机能量，从而点燃旧的神经连接、旧的路径、旧的情感。

sentences.en: It doesn't say anything more than that.
sentences.zh: 这说明不了别的什么。

sentences.en: It is not a secret sign to you to reach out.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是暗示你要去联系对方的秘密信号。

sentences.en: It is not a secret sign that you are not ready for closure, that there is something left to be said.
sentences.zh: 这也不是你还没准备好释怀、还有话没说出口的秘密信号。

sentences.en: It's just likely that something in your environment has subconsciously triggered these memories to reappear.
